title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up the elementary axioms of the topological Euler characteristic, in two versions: ordinary and with compact supports. It is the kind of preliminary one writes before motivic or constructible-function formalisms, or before comparing χ with χ_c in a Gauss–Manin or Picard–Fuchs and 'Cartier operation' context. The dossier context and the reverse side (an administrative typescript) suggest teaching or working notes from Montpellier in the 1970s.

Fix a field k. Two classes of spaces are defined (the subscripts are χ_! and χ, not X):
- E_{χ!} is the class of locally compact spaces X with H^*_!(X,k) = H^*_c(X,k) of finite total dimension. On it, χ_!(X) = Σ(-1)^i dim H^i_c(X,k).
- E_χ is the class of spaces with H^*(X,k) of finite total dimension. On it, χ(X) = Σ(-1)^i dim H^i(X,k).
- The cohomology is first described as sheaf cohomology. This is crossed out and replaced by singular cohomology.

Properties listed:
(a) If X is compact, X ∈ E_{χ!} ⟺ X ∈ E_χ, and then χ_!(X) = χ(X), since H_c = H. Marked 'trivial'.
(b) Let Y be closed in a locally compact X. If two of X, Y, X−Y lie in E_{χ!}, so does the third, and χ_!(X) = χ_!(Y) + χ_!(X−Y). This follows from the long exact sequence H^i_c(X−Y) → H^i_c(X) → H^i_c(Y) → ..., i.e. scissor additivity of χ_c.
(c) Let X', X'' be closed with X' ∪ X'' = X. If three of X, X', X'', X'∩X'' lie in E_χ, so does the fourth, and χ(X) = χ(X') + χ(X'') − χ(X'∩X''). This is inclusion–exclusion from Mayer–Vietoris. A sharpening is added: X, X'∩X'' ∈ E_χ ⇒ X', X'' ∈ E_χ, because H^i(X') ⊕ H^i(X'') sits between finite-dimensional terms of the exact sequence.
(d) Suppose X is homotopy-dominated by X', i.e. there are i: X → X' and r: X' → X with ri = id_X. Then X' ∈ E_χ ⇒ X ∈ E_χ, since H(X) is a direct summand of H(X'). If X ≃ X', the two belong to E_χ together and χ(X) = χ(X').
(e) If Card X ≤ 1 then X ∈ E_χ, with χ(pt) = 1 and χ(∅) = 0.

This is the standard toolkit for computing Euler characteristics by cutting and pasting, or for showing that χ_c is a valuation on suitable subsets.
errors: Property (b) needs the long exact sequence for compact supports attached to an open/closed decomposition. That is valid for sheaf cohomology (Čech or Alexander–Spanier) on locally compact Hausdorff spaces, but not for singular cohomology of arbitrary locally compact spaces. Replacing 'faisceaux' by 'singulière' therefore makes (b) false in general without local niceness hypotheses (e.g. local contractibility, ENR). The crossed-out choice was the correct one for (b).

Property (c), Mayer–Vietoris for a closed cover in singular cohomology, likewise requires an excisive couple, e.g. X', X'' neighbourhood deformation retracts. For sheaf cohomology with closed covers it holds, e.g. on paracompact spaces. Hypotheses are left implicit.

In (d), 'ri = id_X' should presumably read r∘i ≃ id_X (homotopy domination); the strict retract case is a special case. Equality χ(X) = χ(X') is only asserted for homotopy equivalence, which is correct.
Hausdorff hypotheses are implicit throughout, e.g. for H_c = H in (a).

ideas.what: Classes of spaces with finite-dimensional (compactly supported) cohomology, on which χ and χ_c are defined
ideas.modern_name: Euler characteristic / compactly supported Euler characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Euler, Poincaré, Lefschetz; sheaf version Leray, Borel–Moore)

ideas.what: Scissor additivity χ_c(X) = χ_c(Y) + χ_c(X−Y) with two-out-of-three finiteness
ideas.modern_name: additivity of χ_c / Euler characteristic as a motivic measure
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; in algebraic setting Grothendieck/SGA 5 (ℓ-adic), later Kontsevich/Denef–Loeser for motivic measures

ideas.what: Inclusion–exclusion for χ via Mayer–Vietoris, with the sharpening that finiteness for X and X'∩X'' implies it for X', X''
Homotopy domination preserves finiteness; homotopy invariance of χ; normalisation χ(pt) = 1, χ(∅) = 0

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, textbook-level axiomatisation of χ and χ_c (finiteness classes, additivity, Mayer–Vietoris, homotopy invariance, normalisation). It is correct up to standard hypotheses. The only point of interest is that the switch from sheaf to singular cohomology makes (b) and (c) need extra hypotheses. Nothing new to the literature.
transcription_corrections: The class names are 𝓔_{χ!} and 𝓔_χ (subscripts chi-shriek and chi), not 𝓔_{X!} and 𝓔_X; they denote the domains of χ_! and χ.
The margin annotation 'coh. [-faisceaux-] singulière' applies to H^*_!. 'loc. compacts' is inserted after 'espaces topologiques'. The second line is likewise glossed 'coh. singulière'.
The parenthetical in (b) is probably 'résulte de suite exacte de cohomologie à supports quelc.' or 'à s. propres' (uncertain). It is clearly a reference to the long exact sequence for supports.
In (b), 'loc. cpct' is an insertion after 'X', i.e. 'Y fermé dans X loc. cpct'.
In (d) the inserted words are '"domine" homotopiquement par X''. The trailing 'd...' likely begins 'de plus' or 'donc', leading to the X ~ X' statement.
(e): 'qui est un p. ex.' is uncertain; the struck-out text reads roughly 'si X est réduit à un pt', replaced by 'Card X ≤ 1'.
